label: Boyd proposes approximate rational supervenience of actual-case moral judgments
paraphrase: Boyd argues that, to a very good first approximation and by prevailing standards of moral argument, judgments about actual actions, practices and traits are rationally dictated by judgments about nonmoral facts. On a suitable rational reconstruction, disagreements about those moral cases arise from factual disagreements. This is a proposed rational/epistemic dependence under a body of inquiry, not exceptionless sameness of moral properties or a cross-world metaphysical necessity.
